dishes.name: Langar wali Dal (Maa Chole di Dal)

steps: In a bowl mix rice flour, soaked chana dal, peanuts, sesame, onion, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander, chilli powder and salt.
Add hot water little by little and knead into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Divide into 4 balls.
Grease a thick kadai or tawa with 1 tbsp oil. Place a ball in the cold pan and press it out with oiled fingers into a thin round (about 5 mm).
Poke 5–6 holes in the dough with a finger and pour a little oil into each hole.
Cover and cook on medium-low heat 6–8 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.
Flip if you like a crisp top, cook 2 minutes more, and serve hot with chutney or tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix jowar flour and salt; pour in hot water gradually and knead well with the heel of your palm for 3–4 minutes into a smooth dough.
Take a lemon-sized portion, knead it again briefly and pat it out on a floured board into a thin round, turning as you pat.
Lift onto a hot tawa, dry side up. Brush the top with water.
When the water dries (about 1 minute), flip and cook the other side 1 minute.
Flip again and press gently with a cloth, or puff it directly over a flame.
Serve hot with curry, pachadi or red chilli chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Combine flour and salt; add hot water slowly and knead each portion fresh, as bajra dough cracks if left standing.
Pat a ball into a round between your palms or on a floured plastic sheet.
Cook on a hot tawa; brush the top with water and flip when the base sets.
Cook both sides until brown spots appear, pressing the edges with a cloth.
Smear with ghee and serve hot with curry or jaggery.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix corn flour, salt, onion and chilli; knead with hot water into a soft dough.
Pat portions into thick rounds between greased plastic sheets.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa 2–3 minutes per side until spotted brown.
Brush with ghee and serve with spicy chutney or curry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil water with salt; add washed rice and cook until very soft and slightly mushy (about 15 minutes).
Lower the heat and sprinkle in ragi flour, without stirring, so it sits on top. Cover and steam 3 minutes.
Mix vigorously with a wooden spatula until no lumps remain and the mass comes together.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 3–4 minutes more.
Wet your hands, shape into balls, top with ghee and serve with natu kodi pulusu or pappu.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Drain the soaked jowar and coarsely pound or pulse it.
Bring water to a boil, add the jowar and salt, and cook covered on low heat 35–40 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Let it rest 5 minutes; serve with pappu, curd or pickle.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cups basmati or sona masoori rice, soaked 20 min
steps: Heat ghee; add bay leaf, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and shahi jeera and let them crackle.
Add onion and green chillies; fry until light golden.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then add mint and coriander.
Pour in water with salt and bring to a boil.
Add the drained rice, cook on high until most water is absorbed, then cover and cook on low 10 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes and fluff; serve with dalcha, mirchi ka salan or chicken curry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Lemon-sized ball of tamarind, soaked in 3 cups water
steps: Squeeze the tamarind and strain the thin juice into a bowl. (Optional: roast a dry red chilli over a flame and crush it into the juice.)
Add onion, green chillies, jaggery, salt and coriander; stir until the jaggery dissolves.
Heat oil, add mustard, cumin, red chillies, curry leaves and hing; let them splutter.
Pour the tempering into the raw tamarind water — do not cook it.
Serve at room temperature with hot rice and pappu.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pressure-cook mutton with turmeric, half the salt, 1 tsp chilli powder and 1 cup water for 5–6 whistles until tender.
In a little oil, sauté gongura leaves with green chillies until they wilt into a dark mash; grind coarsely.
Heat remaining oil, fry onions until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add remaining chilli powder, coriander powder and salt, then the cooked mutton with its stock; simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the gongura paste and cook 10 minutes more until oil separates.
Finish with garam masala; serve with rice or jonna rotte.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg country chicken (natu kodi), cut in pieces
steps: Marinate chicken with turmeric, salt, chilli powder and ginger-garlic paste for 20 minutes.
Dry-roast coconut, poppy seeds, coriander, cumin, cloves and cinnamon; grind to a smooth paste with water.
Heat oil, add curry leaves and onions and fry until golden.
Add chicken and sear 10 minutes on high, stirring.
Add the masala paste and 2 cups water. Pressure-cook 6–7 whistles (country chicken is tough) or simmer covered 45 minutes.
Simmer open until the gravy is medium-thick; serve with ragi sangati or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Marinate mutton with turmeric, salt and half the ginger-garlic paste for 20 minutes.
Heat oil, fry onions and green chillies until deep golden; add the remaining ginger-garlic paste.
Add mutton and sear on high for 8–10 minutes.
Add chilli and coriander powders, then tomatoes; cook until tomatoes break down.
Add 1.5 cups water and pressure-cook 5–6 whistles.
Simmer to the desired thickness, add garam masala and coriander; serve with rice or rotte.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 goat head, cleaned and cut by the butcher
steps: Wash the pieces well, rub with turmeric and salt and rinse again.
Pressure-cook with turmeric, salt and 3 cups water for 8–10 whistles until the meat is soft.
Heat oil, fry onions until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes and cook down.
Add chilli and coriander powders, then the cooked meat with its stock.
Simmer 15 minutes until thick; finish with garam masala. Serve with rice or rotte.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Scrub the tripe repeatedly with salt and turmeric, rinsing until there is no smell; cut into small pieces.
Pressure-cook with turmeric, salt and 2 cups water for 8–10 whistles.
Fry onions in oil until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook down.
Add spices and the boiled boti; fry 10 minutes, then add some stock and simmer until thick.
Finish with garam masala; serve with rice or rotte.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pressure-cook mutton with turmeric, salt, half the ginger-garlic paste and 1/2 cup water for 5 whistles.
Heat oil, add curry leaves and onion and fry until golden.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste, chilli and coriander powders.
Add the mutton and fry on medium-high, stirring, until all moisture evaporates and the pieces turn dark and dry (15 minutes).
Finish with garam masala and pepper; serve as a side with rice and dal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Marinate chicken with turmeric, salt, chilli powder and ginger-garlic paste for 20 minutes.
Heat oil, add curry leaves, green chillies and onion; fry until golden.
Add chicken and cook covered 10 minutes.
Uncover and fry on medium-high until dry and roasted, 10–12 minutes.
Add coriander powder and garam masala, toss and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fish steaks (murrel, rohu or seer)
Lemon-sized tamarind, soaked in 2 cups water
steps: Rub fish with turmeric, salt and a little chilli powder; rest 15 minutes.
Heat oil, splutter mustard and fenugreek, add curry leaves, onions and green chillies; fry until soft.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, chilli and coriander powders; cook to a paste.
Add the strained tamarind water and simmer 10 minutes.
Slide in the fish pieces and cook on low without stirring for 10 minutes; swirl the pan instead.
Rest the curry an hour before serving with hot rice — it tastes better as it sits.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Small lime-sized tamarind, soaked in 1.5 cups water
steps: Make shallow slits on the eggs and fry them in a little oil with turmeric and chilli powder; set aside.
Splutter mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, onions and green chillies and fry soft.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes; cook until mushy.
Add spice powders and salt, then the tamarind water; simmer 8 minutes.
Add the eggs and simmer 5 minutes more; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g colocasia (arbi), boiled, peeled and halved
Lime-sized tamarind, soaked in 2 cups water
1 tbsp rice flour mixed in water
steps: Splutter mustard and fenugreek in oil; add curry leaves, onion and green chillies and fry soft.
Add the colocasia, turmeric and chilli powder; toss 2 minutes.
Pour in tamarind water with salt and jaggery and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice flour slurry to thicken slightly and simmer 3 minutes.
Serve with hot rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 medium raw mango, peeled and cubed
steps: Pressure-cook toor dal with turmeric and 2.5 cups water for 3 whistles; mash.
Cook raw mango and green chillies in 1/2 cup water until soft (5 minutes).
Add mango to the dal with salt and simmer 5 minutes.
Heat ghee, splutter mustard, cumin, red chillies, garlic, curry leaves and hing; pour over the dal.
Serve with hot rice and ghee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pressure-cook dal, amaranth, tomato, green chillies and turmeric with 2.5 cups water for 3 whistles.
Mash well and add salt.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic and red chilli in oil and pour over.
Serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g raw green tamarind (chintakaya), destringed and chopped
1 tsp fenugreek seeds, roasted and powdered
steps: Lightly sauté green chillies in 1 tbsp oil.
Pound or grind the raw tamarind with chillies, turmeric and salt to a coarse paste (no water).
Mix in fenugreek powder.
Heat the remaining oil, add mustard, chana dal, urad dal, red chillies, garlic and hing; fry until golden.
Pour the tempering over the pachadi and mix. Store in a clean dry jar; serve with hot rice and ghee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 cups gongura (pundi) leaves, washed and dried
steps: Dry-roast coriander, cumin and fenugreek; powder.
Fry green chillies in 1 tbsp oil; remove. Sauté gongura in 1 tbsp oil until it wilts and darkens.
Grind chillies with salt and garlic, then add gongura and spice powder and pulse coarsely.
Temper mustard and red chillies in the remaining oil and mix in.
Serve with hot rice or jonna rotte.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Drain and dry the rice on a cloth for 30 minutes, then grind to a fine flour and sieve.
Mix flour with sesame, ajwain and salt; add water gradually to make a soft, pliable dough.
On a clean cloth, pipe or hand-draw concentric spirals (3–4 rings) of dough with your fingers.
Let the spirals air-dry 20–30 minutes until they can be lifted.
Deep-fry on medium-low heat until crisp and pale golden.
Cool completely and store airtight — a Sankranti festival snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil water with butter, salt, ajwain, chilli powder and moong dal.
Lower heat, add rice flour and stir quickly to form a dough; cover and rest 5 minutes.
Knead well while warm. Roll small portions into thin ropes and join the ends to form rings.
Deep-fry on medium heat until crisp and golden.
Cool and store airtight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flours, cumin, sesame, chilli powder and salt.
Rub in 2 tbsp hot oil, then add water gradually to make a smooth dough.
Fill a murukku press fitted with the star disc and press spirals onto a greased sheet.
Deep-fry on medium heat until the bubbles subside and they turn crisp.
Cool and store airtight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat oil; splutter mustard, chana dal, urad dal and cumin.
Add green chillies, onion and curry leaves; fry until the onion softens.
Add water and salt and bring to a boil.
Pour in rice rava slowly, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook on low 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and cooked.
Garnish with coriander; serve hot with pickle or chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup chickpeas or black-eyed beans, soaked overnight
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked legumes with salt and water for 4 whistles until tender but whole; drain.
Heat oil, splutter mustard, add green chillies and curry leaves.
Add the legumes and toss 2 minutes.
Finish with coconut and lemon juice; serve warm as an evening snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup whole green gram or horse gram, soaked overnight
steps: Boil the soaked gram with salt until just tender; drain.
Temper mustard, cumin, red chillies and curry leaves in oil.
Toss in the boiled gram and coconut; serve — commonly made as a festival offering.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil water with ghee, cumin, salt and soaked chana dal.
Add rice rava gradually, stirring, and cook until it forms a thick mass.
Cool slightly, grease your palms and shape into small balls.
Steam the balls 10–12 minutes in an idli steamer.
Serve with chutney or as a Ganesh Chaturthi offering.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Filling (optional): 1 onion, finely chopped, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp chaat masala
steps: Slit the chillies lengthwise and scrape out seeds.
Mix besan, rice flour, chilli powder, ajwain, soda and salt with water into a thick batter.
Dip each chilli in batter and deep-fry on medium heat until golden.
For stuffed bajji, slit the fried chilli and fill with onion mixed with lemon and chaat masala.
Serve hot with tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub hot ghee and salt into the maida; knead into a firm dough with water and rest 30 minutes.
Mix coconut, roasted gram powder, jaggery, cardamom and cashews for the filling.
Roll small discs, place a spoon of filling, fold into a half-moon and seal; crimp the edges.
Deep-fry on medium-low heat until golden and crisp.
Cool and store — a Diwali and Dasara sweet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Drain the rice, dry on a cloth until just damp, grind to a fine flour and sieve.
Boil jaggery with water to a soft-ball syrup (a drop forms a soft ball in water).
Off the heat, add cardamom and ghee, then add the rice flour gradually, mixing into a soft dough.
Take lemon-sized portions, flatten on greased plastic and sprinkle sesame seeds.
Deep-fry one at a time on medium heat until dark brown.
Press each between two flat ladles to squeeze out excess oil; cool and store.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Tear the warm rotis and pulse them into coarse crumbs.
Mix in jaggery, cardamom and warm ghee by hand.
Add dry fruits and shape into balls or serve loose.
Traditionally offered during Sammakka-Saralamma and Peerla Panduga.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead maida, turmeric and oil with water into a very soft, sticky dough; cover with oil and rest 1 hour.
Pressure-cook chana dal until soft; drain thoroughly.
Cook dal with jaggery until it forms a thick dry mass; add cardamom and grind to a smooth puran. Cool and make balls.
Flatten a ball of dough on greased plastic, place the puran ball in the centre, seal and pat out thin.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden spots appear on both sides; serve warm with ghee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Drain the rice, dry slightly and grind to a fine flour.
Melt jaggery in water and boil to a thick syrup.
Add coconut, cardamom and ghee, then the rice flour; mix into a soft dough-like mass.
Shape into balls — offered to the goddess during Bonalu.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Dry-roast sesame seeds on low heat until they pop and smell nutty; cool.
Melt jaggery with 2 tbsp water and cook to a soft-ball consistency.
Stir in sesame, cardamom and ghee.
Grease hands and shape into small laddus while warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 cups cooked rice, cooled and divided into 4
3 tbsp sesame seeds, roasted and powdered (nuvvula saddi)
2 tbsp lemon juice with 1/2 tsp turmeric (nimmakaya saddi)
steps: Prepare one tempering: heat oil, add mustard, chana dal, urad dal, red chillies, green chillies and curry leaves.
Nuvvula saddi: mix one portion of rice with sesame powder, salt and a quarter of the tempering.
Kobbari saddi: mix the second portion with coconut, salt and tempering.
Nimmakaya saddi: mix the third portion with lemon juice, turmeric, salt and tempering.
Perugu saddi: mix the fourth portion with curd, salt and tempering.
Serve all four together — the traditional offering on the last day of Bathukamma.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup buttermilk (or milk and jaggery for a sweet version)
steps: Whisk ragi flour into 1/2 cup cold water until smooth.
Boil the remaining water, add the slurry and stir continuously on low heat 5–7 minutes until thick and glossy.
Cool, then whisk in buttermilk and salt (or milk and jaggery for sweet java).
Top with onion and serve cool — a summer staple.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cook the flour in water, stirring, until thick (10–12 minutes).
Cool and leave covered overnight to ferment lightly.
Next morning whisk in buttermilk and salt.
Serve with onion and green chilli — offered and drunk during Bonalu.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 cups aged basmati rice, soaked 30 min
1/4 cup milk with a pinch of saffron
Whole spices: 2 bay leaves, 6 cloves, 6 cardamom, 2 inch cinnamon, 1 tsp shahi jeera
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, half the fried onions, half the mint and coriander, green chillies, lemon juice, 3 tbsp ghee and 2 tsp salt. Refrigerate 4–6 hours.
Spread the marinated raw meat in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Boil plenty of water with the whole spices and 1 tbsp salt. Add the rice and cook to 70% done (about 5 minutes); drain.
Layer the rice over the meat; top with remaining fried onions, herbs, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal the lid with dough. Cook on high 5 minutes, then on a tawa over the lowest heat for 50–60 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, open and mix gently from the side; serve with mirchi ka salan and dahi ki chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Saffron soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk
Whole spices: bay leaf, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon, 1 tsp shahi jeera
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices, half the fried onions, herbs, chillies, lemon juice, 2 tbsp ghee and 1.5 tsp salt for 2 hours.
Spread the chicken in a heavy pot.
Par-boil rice with whole spices and salt to 70%; drain and layer over the chicken.
Top with fried onions, herbs, saffron milk and ghee; seal the lid.
Cook 5 minutes on high, then 30–35 minutes on the lowest heat over a tawa.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with salan and raita.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, cauliflower, potato, peas)
Whole spices and 1 tbsp + 1 tsp salt
steps: Marinate vegetables with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices, salt, half the fried onions and herbs for 30 minutes.
Par-boil rice with whole spices and salt to 70%; drain.
Layer vegetables and rice in a pot; top with onions, herbs, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal and cook on dum (low heat over a tawa) 25–30 minutes; rest and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry onions with whole spices until golden.
Add mutton and ginger-garlic paste; sear, then add yogurt, spices and salt.
Pressure-cook with 1 cup water for 4 whistles.
Add remaining water, bring to a boil, add rice and mint.
Cook until water is absorbed, then cover and cook on low 10 minutes; serve with raita.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Large pinch of saffron in 1/4 cup warm milk
Whole spices: 4 cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon, 1 bay leaf
steps: Fry nuts and raisins in ghee; set aside.
Fry whole spices, add rice and toast 2 minutes.
Add water, salt and sugar; cook until 80% done.
Drizzle saffron milk over, cover and cook on dum 10 minutes.
Fluff and garnish with nuts and raisins.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg lamb or whole chicken pieces
Mandi spice: 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, black pepper, cardamom, 1/2 tsp cloves, 1 dried lime (loomi), ground
steps: Rub the meat with mandi spice, salt and ghee; rest 30 minutes.
Roast or slow-cook the meat covered at 160°C for 1.5–2 hours until tender, collecting the juices.
Fry onion in ghee, add tomatoes, some mandi spice and the meat juices plus water to make 5 cups of stock.
Cook rice in the stock until done.
Place a hot charcoal in a small bowl on the rice, drizzle with ghee and cover 10 minutes to smoke.
Serve rice on a large platter topped with the meat and tomato chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/4 cup each chana dal, moong dal, masoor dal, urad dal, soaked
Lemon wedges, fried onions and cashews to garnish
steps: Cook mutton with ginger-garlic paste, chilli, turmeric, yogurt, half the fried onions, mint and salt until very tender; shred the meat and discard bones.
Pressure-cook the wheat and dals with 6 cups water until completely soft.
Combine meat, stock and wheat-dal mixture in a large heavy pot.
Pound continuously with a wooden masher (ghotni) on low heat for 45–60 minutes until stretchy and smooth, adding hot water as needed.
Stir in garam masala and ghee; cook until glossy.
Serve topped with ghee, fried onions, cashews, mint and lemon — the Ramadan classic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 cups whole wheat grains, soaked overnight
steps: Cook the wheat and meat together with salt and plenty of water on low heat until both are very soft (2–3 hours).
Remove bones and beat the mixture vigorously until smooth and porridge-like.
Stir in cinnamon, cardamom and ghee.
Serve with a drizzle of ghee, and sugar if desired.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Khichdi: 1 cup rice, 1/2 cup masoor dal, 1 onion sliced, 2 tbsp ghee, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt
Kheema: 300 g minced mutton, 1 onion, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, 2 tbsp oil
Khatta: lemon-sized tamarind, 2 tbsp sesame seeds, 1 tbsp besan, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 sprig curry leaves, 1/2 tsp cumin
steps: Khichdi: fry onion in ghee, add washed rice and dal, turmeric, salt and 3.5 cups water; cook soft.
Kheema: fry onion, ginger-garlic paste and mince; add spices and a little water and cook dry.
Khatta: roast sesame and grind; cook tamarind water with sesame paste, besan, chilli powder and salt into a thin sour gravy; temper with cumin and curry leaves.
Serve khichdi with kheema and khatta on the side — a Hyderabadi Sunday breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Lime-sized tamarind, soaked in 1 cup water
steps: Slit chillies and fry in oil until blistered; set aside.
Dry-roast peanuts, sesame, coconut, cumin and coriander; grind with the roasted onion and a little water to a smooth paste.
In the same oil splutter mustard, nigella and curry leaves; add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the ground paste, turmeric, chilli powder and salt; fry until oil separates.
Add tamarind water, jaggery and 1/2 cup water; simmer 10 minutes.
Add the chillies and simmer 5 minutes more; serve with biryani.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Same peanut-sesame-coconut paste as mirchi ka salan
steps: Slit brinjals in a cross keeping the stem intact; fry in oil until half cooked.
Grind the roasted peanut-sesame-coconut-onion paste.
Splutter mustard, nigella, fenugreek and curry leaves; add ginger-garlic paste, the paste, turmeric, chilli and salt; fry until oil separates.
Add tamarind water and jaggery; simmer 5 minutes.
Add brinjals, cover and cook until soft; serve with biryani or bagara rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cook tomatoes with 1 cup water until soft; blend and strain.
Whisk besan into a little water and add to the tomato purée with ginger-garlic paste, chilli, turmeric, sugar and salt.
Simmer 15 minutes, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Temper cumin, mustard, red chillies, garlic and curry leaves in oil and pour over.
Add halved eggs if using; serve with khichdi or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Bagaar: 2 tbsp ghee, cumin, 4 dry chillies, 6 garlic cloves, curry leaves
steps: Cook chana dal with turmeric until soft; mash lightly.
Fry onion, add mutton and ginger-garlic paste, spices and salt; pressure-cook with water until tender.
Add bottle gourd, dal and tamarind water; simmer 15 minutes.
Add garam masala and herbs.
Pour the hot bagaar over and serve with bagara khana or biryani.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Bagaar: 2 tbsp oil, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp mustard, 4 dry red chillies, 6 garlic cloves, curry leaves
steps: Pressure-cook dal with turmeric, tomato and green chillies; whisk smooth.
Add tamarind water, chilli powder, salt and water to a pouring consistency; simmer 10 minutes.
Fry the bagaar until the garlic browns and pour over the dal.
Serve with rice and a kebab or fry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp nihari masala (fennel, dry ginger, long pepper, star anise, cardamom, cloves)
2 tbsp wheat flour mixed in water
Ginger juliennes, coriander, lemon to serve
steps: Clean the trotters thoroughly.
Sear meat in ghee with ginger-garlic paste; add spices, fried onion and salt.
Add 10 cups water and slow-cook 5–6 hours (or pressure-cook 1 hour) until gelatinous.
Thicken with the flour slurry and simmer 15 minutes.
Serve with ginger, coriander and lemon alongside kulcha or naan.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pressure-cook trotters with turmeric, salt and 8 cups water for 45 minutes (or simmer 4–5 hours).
Fry onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and spices.
Add trotters and stock; simmer 20 minutes into a thin, rich soup.
Finish with garam masala, coriander and lemon; serve with naan or rotis for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 cup cashews and almonds, soaked and ground
Whole spices: 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon
steps: Fry whole spices in ghee; add mutton and ginger-garlic paste and sear.
Add 6 cups water, green chillies and salt; cook until the mutton is tender.
Whisk yogurt with nut paste and stir in; simmer 10 minutes.
Add milk and white pepper; heat without boiling.
Garnish with mint — served as the first course at Hyderabadi weddings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, nut and coconut paste, fried onions, ginger-garlic paste, spices and salt for 2 hours.
Place in a heavy pot with ghee, seal the lid with dough.
Cook on high 5 minutes, then on dum over a tawa 35–40 minutes.
Stir in cream and serve with naan or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Pickle spices: 1 tsp each fennel, mustard, nigella, cumin, 1/2 tsp fenugreek
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly and crackle the pickle spices.
Add onions and fry golden; add ginger-garlic paste and mutton and sear.
Add yogurt, chilli powder, turmeric and salt; pressure-cook 5 whistles.
Add green chillies and lemon juice; simmer until thick.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry onions until golden, add ginger-garlic paste.
Add kheema and cook on high, breaking lumps, until it changes colour.
Add tomatoes, spices and salt; cook until oil separates.
Add peas and 1/2 cup water; cook covered 15 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and herbs; serve with paratha or khichdi.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g goat offal (tripe, intestines, liver, kidney), cleaned
steps: Scrub the tripe and intestines thoroughly with salt and turmeric; cut small.
Pressure-cook the offal (except liver) for 8–10 whistles.
Fry onions, add ginger-garlic paste and spices, then the boiled offal and liver.
Add stock and simmer; thicken with chana flour.
Finish with garam masala and mint; serve hot, traditionally during Ramadan nights.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g firm fish (murrel or seer), in steaks
steps: Marinate fish with turmeric, chilli powder and salt; lightly shallow-fry and set aside.
Roast sesame, peanuts and coconut; grind with the roasted onion.
Crackle nigella and curry leaves in oil, add ginger-garlic paste and the ground paste; fry until oil separates.
Add tamarind water and simmer 8 minutes.
Add fish and simmer gently 5 minutes; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g boneless mutton, from the leg, sliced thin and flattened
1 onion, sliced into rings, to serve
steps: Marinate the mutton slices with papaya, ginger-garlic paste, spices, lemon juice and salt for 4 hours.
Heat a flat granite stone (or heavy cast-iron griddle) until very hot; grease with ghee.
Cook the slices on the stone, turning once, 4–5 minutes per side until charred at the edges.
Serve with onion rings, lemon and roti.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pressure-cook mutton with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, salt and 1/2 cup water until tender; dry off any liquid.
Toss the pieces with chilli, coriander and garam masala (and a dusting of besan if you like a crust).
Shallow-fry until dark and crisp at the edges.
Serve with khatti dal and rice — the classic pairing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Whole spices: 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon, 6 peppercorns
Filling: 1/2 cup hung curd, 1 small onion finely chopped, 2 green chillies, 2 tbsp mint, 2 tbsp coriander, pinch of salt
steps: Cook mince with chana dal, ginger-garlic paste, whole spices, red chillies, salt and 1 cup water until completely dry.
Grind to a smooth paste; mix in the egg.
Mix the filling ingredients.
Flatten a portion of mince, place a spoon of filling in the centre, seal and shape into a round patty.
Shallow-fry until golden on both sides; serve with onion rings and lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Marinate mutton with all ingredients except ghee for 4 hours or overnight.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal or under a hot grill, basting with ghee, until charred and tender (15–20 minutes).
Serve with onion rings and mint chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Dough: 2 cups maida, 3 tbsp ghee, 1/2 tsp salt, water
steps: Rub ghee into maida and salt; knead into a stiff dough and rest 30 minutes.
Cook mince with onion, ginger-garlic paste and spices until completely dry; add herbs and lemon; cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut into squares.
Place filling on one square, cover with another and seal the edges with a fork.
Deep-fry on medium-low heat until golden and flaky; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken, cut in strips
steps: Marinate chicken with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, cornflour, egg and salt for 20 minutes.
Deep-fry until golden and crisp; drain.
In 2 tbsp oil fry garlic, green chillies and curry leaves.
Add whisked yogurt and garam masala; cook 2 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Toss the fried chicken in the sauce until coated and dry; garnish with coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g boneless fish (basa or murrel), cubed
steps: Marinate fish with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, cornflour, maida, egg and salt for 20 minutes.
Deep-fry until crisp; drain.
In 2 tbsp oil sauté garlic, green chillies and curry leaves.
Add yogurt and soy sauce; cook 1 minute.
Toss in the fish, add lemon juice and serve as a starter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk yogurt until smooth with a little water.
Stir in onion, chillies, herbs, cumin and salt.
Chill and serve with biryani.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 slices white bread, crusts removed, cut in triangles
2 tbsp each sliced almonds, cashews and pistachios
steps: Fry bread in ghee until golden and crisp; drain.
Boil milk and reduce to half (rabri consistency); add saffron and cardamom.
Make a one-string sugar syrup with sugar and water.
Dip the fried bread briefly in syrup and arrange in a dish.
Pour the reduced milk over, simmer 5 minutes so the bread soaks it up.
Garnish with nuts; serve warm or chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g dried Hunza apricots (qubani), soaked overnight in 3 cups water
Fresh cream or malai to serve
steps: Stone the soaked apricots, keeping the soaking water; crack the stones for kernels if desired.
Cook apricots in their water on low heat until soft and broken down (20–25 minutes).
Add sugar and cook until thick and glossy, 10–15 minutes more.
Add lemon juice and kernels.
Serve chilled with cream or malai.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 dates, pitted and sliced, soaked 2 hours
2 tbsp each almonds, pistachios, cashews, sliced
steps: Fry the nuts in ghee; set aside. Fry vermicelli in the same ghee until golden.
Boil milk and simmer 10 minutes.
Add vermicelli and cook until soft.
Add sugar, dates, cardamom, saffron and most of the nuts; simmer 5 minutes.
Serve warm, garnished with nuts — made on Eid morning.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/4 cup basmati rice, soaked and coarsely ground
1 cup bottle gourd (lauki), grated and squeezed
steps: Sauté bottle gourd in ghee until the raw smell goes.
Bring milk to a boil, add ground rice and cook, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Add bottle gourd, khoya, sugar and condensed milk; cook to a thick pudding.
Stir in cardamom and nuts; serve chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk eggs, milk, khoya, sugar and ground almonds until smooth.
Heat ghee in a heavy pan, pour in the mixture and stir continuously on low heat.
Keep stirring 30–40 minutes until it turns grainy, golden and leaves the sides.
Add cardamom and saffron; garnish with nuts — a classic Hyderabadi wedding dessert.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Make a one-string syrup with sugar and water.
Add ground almonds and cook on low heat, stirring, until it forms a soft non-sticky dough.
Add rose water; cool until handleable and knead smooth.
Roll out thin and cut into shapes, imprinting a lattice (jali) pattern with a mould.
Dry overnight; decorate with varq.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 cup sooji or wheat starch (from soaked wheat)
1/2 cup ground nutmeg-flavoured nut mix (almonds, pistachios)
steps: Cook the starch with milk on low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens.
Add sugar and keep stirring; add ghee a spoon at a time.
Continue cooking until the halwa turns translucent and releases ghee.
Stir in nutmeg, saffron and ground nuts.
Set in a greased tray, cool and cut into squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cups bottle gourd, peeled and grated
steps: Sauté grated gourd in ghee 5 minutes.
Add milk and simmer, stirring, until the gourd is soft and the milk reduces by a third.
Add sugar and cardamom; cook 5 minutes.
Garnish with nuts; serve warm or chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Milk with a pinch of saffron for glazing
steps: Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Sift in maida, custard powder, milk powder, salt, baking powder and cardamom; add milk to form a soft dough.
Roll 1 cm thick, cut into rounds and brush with saffron milk.
Bake at 170°C for 18–20 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool and serve with Irani chai — the sweet-salty Hyderabadi café biscuit.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Slice the buns horizontally.
Spread butter generously inside and sprinkle sugar if you like.
Lightly toast on a tawa, cut side down, 1 minute.
Serve with Irani chai for dunking.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Brew a strong decoction: simmer tea leaves in water on very low heat 30–40 minutes.
Separately simmer milk with condensed milk until slightly thickened (dum milk).
Sweeten the decoction with sugar.
Pour 1/3 cup thick milk into each cup and top with 1/3 cup decoction — do not stir before serving.
Serve with Osmania biscuits or bun maska.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook
